newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment unchanged at 9.7 pct in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment unchanged at 9.7 pct in Feb.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate was unchanged at 9.7 in February from January.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.6 percent.
Full time employment fell by 38,000 from the month before, while part time employment grew by 19,300.

Statistics Canada said part-time employment has grown at a faster pace than full-time employment since September. Over the last five months, the number of people with part-time jobs grew 1.2 percent, while full-time employment edged up 0.4 percent, the agency said.
The full-time employment loss in February was concentrated among adult women, who lost 44,000 jobs. Young people also faired poorly in February, with 22,000 fewer people aged 15 to 24 with jobs.
While the number of public sector employees was flat in February, the number of private sector jobs fell by 31,000, Statscan said.
In the retail sector, employment fell by 27,000. Jobs also fell in agriculture, dropping 19,000, said Statscan.
Improvements in transportation, storage and communications helped offset the fall in the other industries, rising by 14,000, the agency said.
The utilities industry gained 7,000 jobs while construction employment was unchanged. Employment in manufacturing has remained flat since October, Statscan said.
